description:
FILED s453 (Fable box-elision review, faster-codegen-suggestions.md par.13 gap 4).  The topic variable keeps the LOOP boxed: `for (1..N) { ... }` always takes boxed p-foreach-range ($_ localized as the dynamic GLOBAL per iteration) even when the accumulator goes raw -- the exact intloop+= bench spelling emits (p-foreach-range ($_ ...) (p-incf-raw $s $_)) and measures 2.07x, while the same loop with an explicit raw counter (cfor) is 0.24x.  FIX SHAPE: a raw topic binding -- bind $_ as a raw per-iteration lexical when the body has NO dynamic $_ reader: no user-sub calls (a called sub may read the global $_), no eval, no goto, no local $_; the front-ends $_-default machinery already rewrites implicit uses (print/uc/regex) to explicit $_ tokens so a lexical binding covers them.  Qualifying bodies are the counting/accumulating loops -- exactly the hot class.  This is the only one of the four par.13 gaps needing a NEW emission (a raw-topic variant of foreach-range-raw); do it LAST, after #758/#759/#760.  Expected: intloop+= 2.07x -> the cfor class (beats perl).  Bar: corpus-diff + full sweep + bench; probe the breaking case (a body that CALLS a sub reading $_) stays boxed.

DONE s456af.  Kind-A gate `raw-topic`.  IT DID NOT NEED THE NEW EMISSION THE TASK PREDICTED, and the measurement is why: 5M iterations, one SBCL image per variant -- special bind + fresh box 0.1680s, special bind + RAW value 0.0160s, plain lexical + raw 0.0150s.  The BOX ALLOCATION is the whole tax; the special bind costs 7%.  So $_ keeps its NAME and its dynamic binding (a callee still sees the element, the outer $_ is still restored) and only the VALUE goes raw; %expand-foreach-range's existing raw arm already applies because %p-cell-loop-var-p answers NIL for the exception-set specials.  No rename, no new macro -- only Parser2::_topic_raw_ok plus a docstring correction in the runtime.  The gate is an ALLOWLIST (a rejected body only loses an optimization): text_gate_tags + a BLANKET rejection of every regex token (a bare //, s/// or tr/// acts on $_ with no `=~` for the gate to see, and two of the three WRITE it) + a short word list with the exclusions documented beside it.  corpus-diff FOUND A HOLE reasoning had missed: perl-tests/closure.t calls $foo[$_]->(4 - $_), and a CODE-REF call carries no Word -- `->` before a List and an `&` Cast are now rejected too (`->` before a Subscript is a deref and stays allowed).  BENCH: intloop+= 2.02x -> 0.28x, intloop= -> 0.29x (both now 3.4-3.6x FASTER than perl), and two rows par.13 did not name because they are topic loops too: arrhash 2.17x -> 1.45x, strcat 3.50x -> ~1.5-2.3x.  53 probes vs perl identical.  RESIDUE, written into the code: overload / tie FETCH / DESTROY are user code reachable with no token to see; such a handler would have to reach the GLOBAL $_ and write through its box to notice.  Guard rows 19-27.
